newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian banks' non-food credit up, says RBI.
newsitem.headline: Indian banks' non-food credit up, says RBI.

text.p: The non-food credit of Indian banks rose by 42.77 billion rupees to 2,546.69 billion rupees during the two weeks ended January 3, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said in its weekly statistical supplement on Monday.
Non-food credit, which mainly represents banks' credit to the industry, was 2,503.92 billion rupees during the fortnight ended December 20, 1996.
"Bank credit is picking up in absolute numbers," said an analyst at a securities firm. "It is a very healthy trend."
"Prima facie it is very impressive," said Prabodh Agarwal, banking analyst at brokerage James Capel B&K.
He said this was the sharpest rise in 1996/97 (April-March).
Overall bank credit (including food credit) rose to 2,632.4 billion rupees on January 3, 1997, from 2,594.1 billion rupees on December 20, 1996, the RBI statement said.
A year ago, banks total credit was 2,389.12 billion rupees as on January 5, 1996.
The year-on-year credit growth fell to 10.2 percent on January 3 from 11.5 percent on December 20, an analyst said.
It was the sharpest year-on-year fall this year, she said.
"Overall, the picture is still not happy," she said.
The RBI had taken several steps late last year to increase funds within the banking system and prompt lending rate cuts to encourage credit offtake from banks.
But banks have reported only moderate pick up in credit.
